newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo bourse retreats on weaker crown, U.S. jitters.
newsitem.headline: Oslo bourse retreats on weaker crown, U.S. jitters.

text.p: Norwegian shares backtracked on Tuesday as the rally on the crown lost momentum and other European markets were hit by the jitters ahead of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to U.S. Congress.
Dealers said investors were seizing the chance to take some profit following this year's bull run, which has seen the Oslo bourse hit 11 all-time closing highs.
The Total share index relinquished 5.57 points, or 0.53 percent, to end the session at 1,038.86 points. Turnover was 1.3 billion crowns.
"The market's generally looking for an excuse to take some profit," said one dealer.
More than two million crowns of total turnover came from the sale by state railway company NSB of its remaining 10 percent stake of tobacco, confectionary and newspaper chain Narvesen.
Offshore group Aker Maritime advanced to an all-time high at 100 crowns before slipping to close at 98 crowns, a rise of four crowns, or almost five percent.
Players said there was much market speculation that Aker Maritime could be announced the winner of a seven billion crown contract for the Aasgard oil and gas project off mid Norway.
